title: 'Sunny Side of the Street' and Lloyd Glenn's piano interlude
summary: Billy Douglas sang and played on the record; the piano interlude was Lloyd Glenn's written idea.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: What about something like where you'd have the piano, I think about Sunny Side of the Street. The piano player is playing the melody, playing his part, and the saxes are playing a background. Do you remember that, your record? Do you remember that part now? It's probably been a long time since you heard it.
Oh, that was the one that Billy Douglas sung and played the trumpet.
Yeah, but there's a little piano part in there.
There's an interlude and he brought Billy Douglas in there. No, Dink Taylor came after the interlude, if I remember.
Yes, that was a written arrangement.
But to me, I never hear many records where the piano stands out over the saxophones. You know, with the saxes in the background. Well, that was a very unusual thing.
It was. It was Lloyd Glenn's idea himself.
Oh, I see. You would work it out together.
